interactions.summary: Jiang endorses the student line that guest-betrayal is especially grave because it attacks chosen trust, hospitality, love, and imagination that make social order possible.
A student raises the special case of a guest betraying the host; Jiang treats it as a real extension of the same hospitality law and says societies could not function without such norms.
The class resumes the canto with the shocking opening of Ugolino's speech, framed by a sinner wiping his mouth on the hair of the head he has been feeding on.

claims.claim: Jiang says the deepest treacheries are judged by how much they damage love and imagination, the forces that hold the universe and society together.
Jiang treats hospitality as a near-universal social law, extending beyond medieval Europe and grounded in the possibility that any guest could be sacred or godlike in disguise.
Jiang says a society without the law of hospitality would lose the basis for contract and ordinary function.
The reading transition to Ugolino emphasizes treachery as bestial repetition: the sinner literally wipes his lips on the hair of the skull he has been chewing.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted Inferno material read in class on 2026-06-24.

signature_moments.moment: A guest might be a god in disguise, so violating hospitality risks offending the divine itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: every guest could potentially be a god in disguise
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It explains why guest-betrayal scales from local offense to cosmic disorder.

signature_moments.moment: Without hospitality there can be no contract and society cannot function.
signature_moments.source_phrase: there could be no basis for any contract
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It translates Dante's ranking into a general theory of civil trust.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The cross-cultural obligation to receive and protect guests, treated here as a foundation of social trust.
Greek mythic logic Jiang uses to explain why betraying a guest can count as sacrilege against the gods themselves.

chronology_notes.note: This packet closes the treachery-ranking discussion and hands the class into the Ugolino episode, which becomes the next major interpretive unit.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student examples are clipped by ASR, but the substantive issue is clear: what happens when the betrayer is the guest rather than the host.
